title: Eval-harness: add “gating mode” output format (structured metrics + confidence intervals + prompt-set revision metadata)
creator: Olivia Grant
description:
Context
Optimize config changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing) will be gated in the control plane. The policy engine needs a deterministic, machine-readable eval result artifact that includes:
- structured metrics (normalized naming + consistent typing)
- confidence intervals / statistical info needed by thresholds
- prompt-set + prompt-set revision metadata (for auditability + cache keys)

This ticket adds a “gating mode” output format to eval-harness. It is intended to be consumed by the async eval runner + policy engine (ENG-3914 / ENG-3913) and surfaced in Console (ENG-3917).

References
- Confluence design: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/optimize-gating-eval-runner-integration.json
- Metric taxonomy/thresholds: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quality-guardrails/guardrails-metric-taxonomy-and-thresholds.json
- Threshold schema ADR (consumer expectations): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-threshold-schema-and-versioning.json

Goals / Non-goals
Goals
1) Produce a single JSON artifact per gating run that can be persisted and evaluated deterministically.
2) Provide sufficient metadata to support result caching and audit logs:
   - model identity + version
   - suite id + suite revision (if applicable)
   - prompt-set id + prompt-set revision
   - config “baseline” vs “candidate” identity
3) Include confidence intervals and sample sizes per metric.

Non-goals
- Define threshold logic (policy engine owns that).
- Replace existing eval-harness output formats; gating mode should be additive.

Proposed output format (v1)
The gating artifact is a single JSON document written by eval-harness in addition to any existing human-readable output.

Top-level fields (required unless stated otherwise):
- schema_version: string (e.g., "redwood.gating_eval.v1")
- run_id: string (passed through from runner)
- created_at: RFC3339 timestamp
- eval_harness_version: string
- suite_id: string
- suite_tags: array of strings (e.g., ["chat", "tool-calling", "structured-output", "quantization"]) (optional but recommended)
- prompt_set_id: string
- prompt_set_revision: string (git sha / content hash)
- prompt_set_ref: string (human-friendly ref; optional)
- baseline:
  - model_id: string (e.g., "llama-3.1-70b")
  - model_version: string (Redwood serving version or upstream commit)
  - runtime_profile: string (optional; e.g., "fp16", "int8-awq")
  - config_fingerprint: string (hash of relevant serving config)
- candidate: same fields as baseline
- sample_size: integer (effective count used for aggregated metrics)
- metrics: array of metric objects

Metric object fields:
- name: string (taxonomy-aligned; examples below)
- kind: string enum: "higher_is_better" | "lower_is_better" | "binary_rate" | "continuous_score"
- unit: string (e.g., "score", "rate", "tokens")
- baseline_value: number
- candidate_value: number
- delta: number (candidate - baseline)
- ci_method: string (e.g., "bootstrap_percentile", "wilson", "student_t")
- ci_level: number (e.g., 0.95)
- baseline_ci_low / baseline_ci_high: number (optional; required when available)
- candidate_ci_low / candidate_ci_high: number (optional; required when available)
- delta_ci_low / delta_ci_high: number (optional; required when available)
- n: integer (per-metric sample size if differs from top-level sample_size)
- notes: string (optional; e.g., grader model version, rubric)

Example metric names (aligning with taxonomy):
- "task.success_rate"
- "rubric.overall_score"
- "safety.toxicity_rate"
- "format.json_valid_rate"
- "tool_call.valid_rate"

Implementation notes / decisions
- Determinism: metrics array MUST be sorted by metric name ascending to avoid downstream non-determinism in hashing/caching and policy evaluation.
- Floating point: round to a fixed precision in the JSON output (proposal: 6 decimal places) to avoid tiny drift across platforms.
- Confidence intervals:
  - For binary rates: Wilson interval @ 95%.
  - For continuous scores: bootstrap percentile @ 95% with fixed seed.
  - For delta CI: compute from paired bootstrap samples when feasible; otherwise omit delta CI but include baseline/candidate CI.
- Minimum sample sizes: include n fields; do not enforce min sample size in eval-harness (policy engine enforces).
- Backward compatibility: gating mode is enabled via a CLI flag or config: --output-format=gating_v1 (name bikeshed below).

CLI / API
- Add an output writer: gating JSON written to a known path (runner will supply), e.g.:
  --gating-output-path=/artifacts/gating_summary.json
- Add a switch:
  --mode=gating (or --gating-mode)
  In gating mode we:
  - emit the gating JSON
  - enforce metric name normalization
  - error if prompt_set_revision is missing

Acceptance criteria
1) New gating output JSON passes schema validation tests (unit tests in eval-harness).
2) Output includes prompt_set_revision and is stable across reruns with same seed and inputs.
3) Metrics are sorted and include n + CI fields per the chosen method.
4) Runner integration can parse the artifact without custom per-suite logic.
5) Documented in eval-harness README / internal doc (short section describing fields + versioning).

Open questions (to resolve before merge)
- Naming: --mode=gating vs --output-format=gating_v1. (Preference: --mode=gating + schema_version in artifact.)
- For continuous metrics: do we standardize on bootstrap only, or allow t-interval when assumptions hold?
- Do we include per-prompt breakdowns? (Leaning no; store separately as optional artifacts; gating summary should stay small.)

Work plan
- Implement JSON schema struct + serializer
- Add CI calculators (Wilson, bootstrap w/ fixed seed)
- Add schema validation + golden tests
- Update docs

Progress / activity
2025-01-17 (Olivia Grant)
- Drafted schema fields with Sana Farid + Selene Huang; agreement that prompt_set_revision is mandatory and must be part of cache key.

2025-01-22 (Sana Farid)
- Stats feedback: use Wilson for rates; bootstrap for rubric scores. Require ci_level included explicitly to avoid ambiguity.

2025-01-24 (Jordan Lee)
- Policy engine request: ensure metrics are normalized and sorted; also include config_fingerprint for baseline/candidate so we can trace “what changed” even if the high-level proposal is identical.

2025-01-28 (Logan Wright)
- Telemetry note: keep gating summary artifact small; store per-case outputs separately to avoid huge payloads in audit events.

2025-02-03 (Olivia Grant)
- Implemented gating writer + golden tests. Added deterministic sorting + numeric rounding to 6 decimals. Added bootstrap with fixed seed derived from (run_id, metric_name).

2025-02-06 (Olivia Grant)
- Merged and tagged release.

Links
- GitHub (eval-harness): sources/github/eval-harness/pr_912.json (implements gating output format + CI computation)
- Follow-up suite selector helpers: sources/github/eval-harness/pr_927.json

Risks / follow-ups
- Bootstrap runtime cost: ensure we do not blow up eval runtime for large suites; follow-up to add configurable bootstrap iterations with sensible default (currently 1k). If perf becomes an issue, policy engine can accept baseline/candidate CI only and omit delta CI.
- Ensure downstream handles missing delta CI gracefully.

Definition of Done
- PR merged in eval-harness
- Release cut and communicated to eval runner implementers (ENG-3914)
- Runner integration smoke-tested in staging with one quantization gating suite and one structured-output suite
